plannedSlices.notes: Re-scoped active RMG work away from owner-H3M sample-by-sample exact-count fitting. Added docs/native-rmg-generalized-policy-regate-audit.md, which records exact counts as diagnostics only, identifies owner-specific runtime branches as temporary fixture/diagnostic debt, and defines the next implementation direction around generalized template/profile policy, zone graph semantics, town/guard/blocker route closure, road materialization, water/underground policy, and corpus subsystem grouping. Earlier local Small-islands count-fitting edits were abandoned before commit; uploaded/generated map evidence remains untracked. Owner-corpus report schema v6 now emits generalized_policy_failure_summary alongside raw exact deltas; after native rebuild, the raw mapped gate remained 8/9 while the active Small islands failure was grouped into guard_policy, town_policy, decoration_blocker_policy, object_density_policy, and object_reward_policy. Added runtime_policy_classification to native RMG output/report/provenance/metadata and updated the auto-template batch report to require it while guarding normal generated seeds against seed-specific owner overrides. Added explicit generated-map level selection using Surface Only (1 Level) and Surface + Underground (2 Levels), and corrected one-level scoped islands terrain so underground terrain appears only on requested two-level maps. Fixed the Small normal-water two-level owner-corpus package reflow so player start towns remain on their generated start anchors, then made native town placement level-aware so the owner Small normal-water two-level path preserves four surface towns plus one underground supplemental town. The owner corpus now improves to 7/9 mapped pass; remaining mapped failures are Small islands two-level and XL no-water. Added fast non-Godot RMG audit tooling so H3M/native package validation no longer depends on a full Godot startup; Godot remains for generation/adoption/editor/runtime integration only. Small islands two-level work also corrected level-aware object/guard/town pathing defects exposed by the focused diagnostic, while broad production parity remains in progress. Focused Small islands two-level validation now passes in a narrow Godot integration smoke; the slow full Godot owner-corpus parser loop is no longer the recommended tight validation path. Fast audit batch mode now parses the whole uploaded owner H3M corpus and local native AMAP evidence without Godot, providing a corpus-level baseline for the next generalized RMG policy fixes. Native batch export now isolates the single Godot-required generation step from Python-side corpus comparison; the resulting generated batch confirms broad object-density underfill on large two-level maps and sets the next generalized policy target. Generalized catalog-auto generation now fixes the first generated-batch rule failures with size/level-aware density floors, eligible underground decoration/scenic and road distribution, strict town-spacing/same-zone town guards, and targeted batch export; a full 18-case export passes the fast Python generated-rule gate with zero density gaps and zero native rule failures. A broader fast policy gate now fails that same batch with 14 guard/object/town/road/guard-reward policy gaps, keeping the active slice correctly in progress instead of accepting structural package validity as production readiness. Native catalog-auto scenic-object and guard floors reduce that policy gap count to 5 on combined 18-package evidence; the generated guard floor now also raises stale fixture caps for normal non-owner-discovered catalog-auto packages, the Small two-level road floor raises road density to 116 cells per targeted package, and the fast policy epsilon clears sub-tile road-density noise. Generated two-level neutral-town floors clear the remaining density/category policy gaps. The fast validator now adds a road-topology gate; generalized road component materialization now clears that gate on fresh 18-package evidence with 0 topology gaps. Normal generated Large/XL land seeds no longer activate owner-specific land profile overrides; the XL one-level road floor now keeps 144x144_l1 above the fast policy floor without that override. The object-category floor now raises normal catalog-auto scenic/other-object density before decorative filler, and the fast policy gate requires at least 60% of owner object-category density. The Godot auto-template report is retained as an integration smoke, but slow Godot parser/comparison reports are not part of the tight correctness loop. Full production parity remains in progress. Medium two-level islands category caps now exact-match broad owner counts while preserving route, road, and town deltas at zero; production_ready remains false because terrain/road-component and other profile gaps remain. Medium two-level normal-water route/terrain cleanup reduced focused production-gap severity to 96 and kept merged 18-case Python gates clean; production_ready remains false because guarded-route, road-component, town capacity, and other profile gaps remain. Medium two-level islands terrain cleanup reduced focused terrain-blocked delta to +3 and kept merged 18-case Python gates clean; production_ready remains false because road-component, guard-footprint, XL/Large terrain, and route-shape gaps remain. Large two-level islands terrain cleanup reduced focused severity to 145 and kept route deltas at 0/0; merged 18-case Python gates remain clean while production_ready remains false. XL two-level normal-water package guard-shape cleanup matched owner physical object-route openness at 16/16, improved guarded-route openness from 0/10 to 2/10, reduced focused severity from 417 to 356, and kept merged 18-case Python gates clean while production_ready remains false. XL two-level land category/underground cleanup reduced xl_nowater_2levels severity from 367 to 47, brought total object/category/terrain deltas near owner evidence, and kept merged 18-case Python gates clean while production_ready remains false. XL two-level normal-water town/terrain cleanup now reaches owner town count/split at 16/16 with 11/5 surface/underground towns, keeps object-route openness at 16/16, reduces focused severity from 356 to 263, and keeps merged 18-case Python gates clean; production_ready remains false because guarded-route openness is still 3/10 versus owner 10/10 and broader parity gaps remain. Large two-level normal-water category/terrain cleanup reduced l_normalwater_randomplayers_2level severity from 342 to 55, category absolute delta from 144 to 13, terrain delta to +5, and kept merged 18-case Python gates clean; production_ready remains false because l_nowater_randomplayers_nounder route shape is now the top blocker. completionCriteria: Define typed MapDocument and ScenarioDocument boundaries with explicit schema/version, stable ids, metadata, terrain/layer data, object placements, route/validation metadata, and generated provenance.

currentInspectionFindings: RandomMapGeneratorRules.generate(input_config) returns large nested Dictionary payloads with scenario_record, metadata, staging, validation/report, and provenance rather than a typed map object.

ScenarioSelectRules launches generated skirmishes by handing the generated payload to ScenarioFactory.create_generated_skirmish_session(...), preserving no-authored-writeback and memory/session-only boundaries.
Authored scenarios are bundled in content/scenarios.json with scenario metadata, terrain rows, objectives, script hooks, and placements in one JSON domain.
SaveService._save_raw_dictionary() serializes full payload dictionaries with JSON.stringify(payload, "\t") and writes raw JSON strings through FileAccess.
A Small 36x36 generated map profile wrote about 6.95 MB of JSON and measured roughly 202-219 ms in the save path, so full-payload JSON saves are already expensive before larger maps.

plannedSlices.purpose: Improve onboarding, tooltips, town planning clarity, battle intent feedback, save/load confidence, and reduce debug-like seams.
plannedSlices.summary: Completed bounded player-comprehension polish. Overworld and town use responsive compact layouts at 1280x720; at 1024x600 the town opens scenery-first and a footer switch exposes the full-width order board without losing management access. Generated-skirmish setup and Load use player-readable workflows without recovery or file-integrity internals. Fresh expeditions open on a safe suggested route with an enabled order. Town construction uses a two-step plan/confirm workflow with exact cost, readiness, impact, trade handoff, and non-mutating selection. Battle places the scored suggested order and expected damage, retaliation, range, momentum, or posture consequence directly in the existing command rail. Focused generated-setup, save/load, lean-boot save, first-turn, town-planning, and battle-intent validation passed; the earlier broad battle-layout matrix remains explicitly unclaimed.
plannedSlices.title: UX Polish Player Comprehension

implementation: Overworld compact mode removes duplicate briefing, commitment, route-cue, and resource rails while retaining resources in the status tooltip; narrow mode preserves map, order, end-turn, save, and menu actions.

Town compact mode prioritizes the authored town stage and selected management tab; narrow mode opens scenery-first and exposes a Town Orders/View Town footer switch between the full-width stage and full-width management surface.
Responsive state is reapplied after overworld refresh so hidden secondary rails do not reappear during play.

Generated-skirmish setup replaces recovery/debug vocabulary with a map plan, supported Land/Surface scope, Build & Play action, readable build/check stages, actionable setup failure recovery, and an explicit no-save-change guarantee.

Generated-map UI tests now reject internal/provenance/template/profile/retry/validation terms in visible setup and failure copy while retaining hidden native authority metadata for runtime validation.
The main-menu Load board replaces play-check, resume-handoff, integrity, internal id, and coordinate diagnostics with concise saved-expedition rows and a destination-specific resume preview.
Latest is prefixed so it remains visible when rows clip at 1024x600; the selected preview and Resume Expedition command remain fully inside both validated viewports.
Load refreshes the selected slot immediately before routing. A removed or unreadable save stays on the menu, disables the action, explains the failure, and leaves saved slots unchanged.

Fresh first-turn sessions select the nearest reachable visible player town, then an uncollected resource or artifact as deterministic non-combat fallbacks, and immediately expose the destination-specific primary order.
Opening route suggestion is UI-only: focused coverage proves day, hero position, movement, and resources remain unchanged, while map clicks or committed actions clear the suggestion state.

The suggested destination does not auto-open the contextual Tile drawer; 1280x720 capture keeps the right rail compact with Visit Town enabled, while 1600x900 pairs the same order with the one-shot briefing.
Responsive breakpoints use the containing viewport when the shell has no parent Control, preventing drawer content from changing its own layout mode.
Build options now select a construction plan instead of committing immediately; ready, trade-coverable, and blocked options remain inspectable from the same list.

The selected build preview exposes exact cost, readiness, strategic impact, and a non-mutating selection guarantee; a separate primary Build command performs the irreversible spend, while market-coverable plans route to Trade.

Focused multi-size coverage proves selection preserves buildings and resources, confirmation adds exactly the chosen building and spends resources, and the 1024x600 Town Orders switch keeps both management and scenic return commands inside the frame.
Existing town entity-cache automation and the broader town/battle visual smoke continue to execute and validate the direct construction commit path.

The battle action guide now renders the scored Suggested order and expected consequence from the existing read-only intent payload as its first line, while retaining position and objective checks below it.

Advance previews omit green-hex tutorial wording from the visible consequence so range, momentum, obstruction, cover, contact, and objective effects receive the limited command-rail space; deeper interaction guidance remains in tooltips.
Strike and Shoot previews surface live damage, unit-loss, and retaliation ranges; enemy initiative surfaces the incoming order without implying player control.

The focused intent test preserves scored tactical-order selection, target identity, expected damage, risk, confidence, and non-mutation, while the broader town/battle smoke rejects visible Try/click instructions and requires the exact forecast line on-screen.
